N1.risk_note: Cheap on GPU (about 4 cells incl. a missing Llama no-channel baseline); risk is only that open models ignore the screen, which is still a reportable result.

N2.risk_note: Sonnet cells cost up to 7 USD each; run threshold 5 and unannounced on Sonnet no channel plus Haiku. Turns the focal-price anecdote into a causal monitor-gaming result.

N3.risk_note: Qwen fine paraphrase is cheap; one Sonnet fine cell about 7 USD. If it fails again, the fine finding weakens, but honestly so.

N4.risk_note: Leniency forms about 10 cartels per 4 pools; 4 more pools add a handful, not enough to change any cartel-level conclusion.

N5.risk_note: Uninstructed Sonnet already prices exactly at the announced threshold, so evasion is largely shown; new design in a day, dual-use framing needs care.

why: N2 tests whether an announced detector threshold becomes the target, the most safety-relevant claim; N1 shows the screen across three families cheaply; N3 shores up wording robustness. About 24 USD API, 3 USD GPU, leaving rewrite time.
missing_run: An evaluation-awareness arm: Haiku laissez-faire and fine framed as a real deployment for a named firm, to test whether cartel and deterrence behaviour are artefacts of the experiment framing.
